name: soybean lipoxygenase-1 (SLO, WT-SLO)
notes: Paper gives no EC number; 1.13.11.12 is the EC of UniProt P08170 (LOX1_SOYBN). Recombinant enzyme expressed from the pT7-7 plasmid in E. coli. PDB: the paper cites the structure of Minor et al. (ref 36) without an entry code; the listed entries are those UniProt cross-references for P08170 (looked up 2026-11-10) for which RCSB gives no mutation and an 839-residue entity. Not listed: 4WFO (Mn-substituted, 858-residue construct), 1Y4K (title says N694G although the mutation field is empty) and all entries with engineered mutations. Table 1 marks the row WT-SLO with footnote e (Rickert & Klinman, Biochemistry 1999, 38, 12218).

name: soybean lipoxygenase-1 (SLO)
notes: Named 'Leu546 -> Ala' in the paper; numbering of P08170. Mutant prepared by QuikChange and sequenced (ref 18); Table 1 marks the row with footnote e (Rickert & Klinman 1999) and Methods state that the L546A data appeared in that earlier publication. PDB 5TQN (L546A, 293 K) per RCSB mutation field; the double mutant entries 4WHA/5TQO are not listed.

name: soybean lipoxygenase-1 (SLO)
notes: Named 'Leu754 -> Ala' in the paper; mutation confirmed by sequencing ~500 bp around the site. Deuterated substrate for this mutant was 2H31-linoleic acid; assayed at 1-20 uM LA because of substrate inhibition. PDB 5TR0 (L754A, 293 K) per RCSB mutation field.

name: soybean lipoxygenase-1 (SLO)
notes: Named 'Ile553 -> Ala' in the paper; mutation confirmed by sequencing ~500 bp around the site. PDB 3BNE (I553A); RCSB lists for this entry, besides I553A, the difference S160E, which this study did not engineer.

name: dihydrofolate reductase (ecDHFR)
notes: Paper gives no EC number; 1.5.1.3 is the EC of UniProt P0ABQ4 (DYR_ECOLI, strain K12). The communication names neither strain nor expression construct ('wild-type ecDHFR'; enzyme from the Benkovic laboratory, co-authors). pdb left empty: UniProt cross-references more than 150 PDB entries for P0ABQ4 (looked up 2026-11-10), too many to vet, and the paper names no PDB entry.

name: alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH-hT)
organism: Bacillus stearothermophilus strain LLD-R (now Geobacillus stearothermophilus)
notes: Paper gives no EC number; 1.1.1.1 is the EC of UniProt P42328 (ADH3_GEOSE, 'ADH-HT'). Thermophilic ADH from the LLD-R strain, 'expressed and purified as described before (refs 10, 11) with minor modification'. The paper (1999) names no PDB entry; 1RJW (2004) is the structure of the ADH of B. stearothermophilus strain LLD-R without mutation per RCSB; 3PII carries L176F and is not listed.

name: thymidylate synthase (ecTS, TS)
notes: EC 2.1.1.45 is printed by the paper (first line of the Introduction) and is the EC of UniProt P0A884 (TYSY_ECOLI). Expression system a gift from R. Stroud (UCSF); enzyme produced and purified by a published procedure (ref 47); wild type ('wild-type ecTS', Conclusions). pdb left empty: UniProt cross-references about 67 PDB entries for P0A884 (looked up 2026-11-10), too many to vet, and the paper names no entry.

name: yeast alcohol dehydrogenase (YADH)
notes: Commercial enzyme: '800 U/ml YADH (Boehringer Mannheim Biochemicals)'. The paper names neither species, isozyme nor EC number; assigned to S. cerevisiae ADH1 (UniProt P00330, EC 1.1.1.1), the fermentative isozyme that commercial baker's-yeast ADH consists of - this assignment is mine, not the paper's. PDB entries are those UniProt cross-references for P00330 (looked up 2026-11-10), all without mutation and 347 residues per RCSB; sequences were not compared residue by residue with P00330 (commercial yeast ADH can differ from the S288c sequence at a few positions). The paper (1989) cites only horse-liver ADH and DHFR structures.
